title: Trump’s Battle with the Fed Explained | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 25
summary: Former Dallas Fed president Robert Kaplan explains the tension between weak hiring and inflation, the case for a quarter-point September rate cut, and how policymakers use business contacts. The conversation moves to tariffs, factory investment, merger integration, Goldman’s client strategy and bank consolidation. Eisman explicitly agrees with the 25-basis-point call and advances a technology-scale argument for bank mergers.
assessment: The September 2025 rate-cut forecast is a clear bounded success for Kaplan and for Eisman’s explicit endorsement. Most claims about private Fed deliberations, business sentiment and the causes of inflation remain insufficiently identified for a binary outcome grade. Kaplan’s claim that Goldman eliminated client conflicts is contradicted by the firm’s own risk disclosures. His management views and merger recommendations remain separate from Eisman’s forecasts.
framework_points: Ask how a policy affects labor supply, prices, investment timing and business margins separately.
Use business contacts as a complement to economic releases while recognizing selection and revision risk.
Separate a completed merger agreement from the integration that creates or destroys value.
Compare fee-oriented client businesses with principal risk and check whether conflicts are managed rather than assumed absent.
Treat bank technology scale and consolidation as hypotheses requiring franchise and competition evidence.
tools_and_charts: Dual mandate, labor-force supply, inflation measures and the estimated neutral policy rate.
FOMC voting structure and the role of regional business outreach.
Tariff-sensitive import margins, housing affordability and factory expensing.
Merger integration, client franchises, capital requirements and stress testing.
Bank size distribution, deposit competition and public-debt/GDP definitions.
transcript_cautions: Read every caption segment through the closing disclosure.
Opening preview repeats later passages and is not counted as extra claims.
Kaplan supplies most substantive answers; Eisman’s questions do not automatically endorse them. His 25-basis-point prediction is an explicit exception.
The source refers to the September 2025 FOMC decision prospectively. Goldman/T. Rowe Price collaboration was announced September 4; an exact recording date is not asserted.
Captions confuse names and contain an inconsistent return-to-Goldman year. Incidental career chronology is not used as an investment forecast.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Robert Kaplan. Kaplan owns his policy, management and Goldman assessments; Eisman’s explicit comments and adoptions are separately recorded.

claims.test: Distinguish eligible directors from bank-affiliated Class A directors.
claims.reason: The official process supports Kaplan’s correction; only Class B and C directors participate in this appointment.

evidence.title: Selection of Reserve Bank presidents
evidence.finding: Class B and C Reserve Bank directors appoint the president, subject to Board of Governors approval. It is not a presidential appointment.

claims.claim: US growth is around 1.25%-1.5%, and low unemployment partly reflects declining labor supply.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Identify the vintage, growth window, participation measure and immigration adjustment.
claims.reason: The growth period and labor-supply series are not specified. A first-half annualized growth estimate is not interchangeable with quarterly annualized or year-over-year GDP.
claims.next_check: Identify the vintage, growth window, participation measure and immigration adjustment.

claims.claim: Labor supply has collapsed.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define the relevant labor-supply flow or stock and compare it with official estimates.
claims.reason: Eisman intensifies the guest’s description without a quantitative series or timeframe. It should not be converted into a claim that all US employment has collapsed.
claims.next_check: Define the relevant labor-supply flow or stock and compare it with official estimates.

claims.claim: Tariffs and uncertainty over undocumented workers are near-term growth headwinds even if reshoring eventually helps.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare labor availability, investment and output with an explicit counterfactual.
claims.reason: These are plausible channels, but their net contribution is not isolated from other shocks. The stated 10-15 million undocumented-worker range is not independently established here.
claims.next_check: Compare labor availability, investment and output with an explicit counterfactual.

claims.claim: Factories cannot be built overnight, so reshoring cannot immediately offset a trade shock.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.
claims.reason: The implementation-lag point is useful, but no specific factory schedule or quantified output gap is forecast.
claims.next_check: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.

claims.claim: Regulatory review, energy development and AI data-center investment should support growth.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Track completed investment, capacity utilization and incremental output.
claims.reason: The directional thesis lacks an exact horizon, project set or GDP increment. Announcements alone cannot establish the ultimate productive return.
claims.next_check: Track completed investment, capacity utilization and incremental output.

claims.claim: The Fed must balance employment and price stability rather than simply maximize next year’s GDP growth.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare policy reasoning with the statutory mandate and official statement.
claims.reason: The FOMC statement confirms the employment and inflation objectives and balancing of risks. This is institutional explanation, not a return forecast.

evidence.title: September 17, 2025 FOMC statement
evidence.finding: The committee cut its target range by 25 basis points to 4%-4.25%, citing slower job gains and elevated inflation.

claims.next_check: Compare policy reasoning with the statutory mandate and official statement.

claims.claim: Inflation is roughly 2.75%-3%, with sticky services and added goods pressure from tariffs.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Match the discussion to the then-available inflation release and components.
claims.reason: The magnitude depends on CPI versus PCE, headline versus core and release vintage. The source does not consistently specify which series each figure describes.
claims.next_check: Match the discussion to the then-available inflation release and components.

claims.claim: Tariff inflation is likely to be mainly a one-time level adjustment.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Measure pass-through and subsequent inflation after controlling for other price shocks.
claims.reason: A one-time price-level effect differs from repeated tariff changes, indirect wage effects and inflation expectations. No precise tariff path or persistence test is specified.
claims.next_check: Measure pass-through and subsequent inflation after controlling for other price shocks.

claims.claim: Labor-market weakness will lead the Fed to cut 25 basis points in September 2025.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare the September meeting decision with the forecasted magnitude.
claims.reason: The September 17 decision reduced the target range by exactly 25 basis points. The outcome supports the stated meeting forecast, not every causal premise.

evidence.title: September 17, 2025 FOMC statement
evidence.finding: The committee cut its target range by 25 basis points to 4%-4.25%, citing slower job gains and elevated inflation.

claims.next_check: Compare the September meeting decision with the forecasted magnitude.

claims.claim: A real neutral rate around 0.75% implies nominal neutral near 3.5%, leaving only 75-100 basis points of easing room.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Identify expected inflation and the neutral-rate model; test a range rather than a point estimate.
claims.reason: The addition is arithmetically valid under the chosen inflation assumption, but neutral is an uncertain estimated equilibrium, not an observed policy target. Current inflation need not equal expected equilibrium inflation.
claims.next_check: Identify expected inflation and the neutral-rate model; test a range rather than a point estimate.

claims.claim: Political pressure is not being discussed inside the FOMC and does not determine members’ policy choices.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Use contemporaneous meeting records and attributable testimony without inferring motive from a rate move.
claims.reason: Kaplan is describing his expectations and past experience, not reporting verified access to every current deliberation. Public decisions cannot identify private motives.
claims.next_check: Use contemporaneous meeting records and attributable testimony without inferring motive from a rate move.

claims.claim: Fed staff should focus on the mandate and ignore political pressure, even when criticism is inevitable.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.
claims.reason: This is a professional norm and a description of the ethic Kaplan favors, not a measurable guarantee about all officials.
claims.next_check: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.

claims.claim: With all seats filled, 19 policymakers participate and 12 vote, with regional presidents rotating.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Account for vacancies and distinguish participation from voting rights.
claims.reason: The official structure gives seven governors and twelve Reserve Bank presidents, with twelve votes and New York permanently voting.

evidence.title: FOMC voting membership
evidence.finding: Up to seven governors, New York’s president and four rotating Reserve Bank presidents vote. The other seven presidents participate without a vote.

claims.next_check: Account for vacancies and distinguish participation from voting rights.

claims.claim: The chance that an official supports a cut simply to appease the president is effectively zero.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Seek direct, attributable evidence of decision criteria rather than infer private intent.
claims.reason: This is a strong claim about unobserved motives. Kaplan explicitly lacks proof that dovish officials are seeking promotion; the same uncertainty prevents establishing a zero probability.
claims.next_check: Seek direct, attributable evidence of decision criteria rather than infer private intent.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the specific meeting’s target-range change.
claims.reason: This is his explicit adoption of the guest’s bounded call, and the September 17 decision matched it. It is not credited merely because he hosted Kaplan.

evidence.title: September 17, 2025 FOMC statement
evidence.finding: The committee cut its target range by 25 basis points to 4%-4.25%, citing slower job gains and elevated inflation.

claims.next_check: Compare the specific meeting’s target-range change.

claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare payroll vintages, revisions and a representative business survey.
claims.reason: Business conversations are selective and the data vintage matters. The eventual size of the cut does not independently prove the assessment of every business or the counterfactual policy optimum.
claims.next_check: Compare payroll vintages, revisions and a representative business survey.

claims.claim: Tariff uncertainty has caused businesses to pull back despite an otherwise acceptable economy.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Test investment and hiring plans against exposure to policy uncertainty.
claims.reason: Eisman reports what contacts have told him; the causal effect is not quantified or independently isolated.
claims.next_check: Test investment and hiring plans against exposure to policy uncertainty.

claims.claim: The new tax law lets a US factory investment be written off fully.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Apply the eligibility rules and distinguish deduction from tax-credit value.

evidence.finding: Qualified production property can receive 100% depreciation under construction and placed-in-service conditions following the 2025 law; it is a deduction, not reimbursement of the entire construction cost.

claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare the contemporary dissent with the later account.

claims.claim: If neutral rises while the policy rate remains fixed at zero, policy becomes more accommodative relative to neutral.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Estimate neutral separately and compare the real policy-rate gap.
claims.reason: This is a conditional policy-gap relationship. It does not prove how much neutral actually rose or quantify the subsequent inflation effect.
claims.next_check: Estimate neutral separately and compare the real policy-rate gap.

proof.derivation: Policy gap = actual real rate - neutral real rate. Holding the actual rate fixed while neutral rises makes the gap more negative.

claims.claim: After publicly disagreeing, a policymaker should accept the group’s decision without pretending to know the correct future rate path.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.

claims.next_check: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.

claims.claim: Extraordinary fiscal stimulus combined with highly accommodative monetary policy turned supply-driven inflation into excess-demand inflation.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare fiscal impulses, supply recovery, monetary conditions and a defensible inflation decomposition.
claims.reason: The mechanism is plausible, but the relative contribution and no-stimulus counterfactual are not identified here. Package headline sizes also differ from timing of actual demand effects.
claims.next_check: Compare fiscal impulses, supply recovery, monetary conditions and a defensible inflation decomposition.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.next_check: Compare sector productivity, labor displacement, prices and competing explanations.

claims.claim: Goldman now commits capital more for clients and conducts much less proprietary trading than before the crisis.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan

claims.claim: Goldman has eliminated client conflicts because capital commitments are always on behalf of clients.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare the absolute assertion with risk disclosures and actual transaction structures.
claims.reason: Goldman’s own annual filing describes ongoing potential conflicts involving client services and its investments, and warns that cross-division collaboration can increase them. Managing conflicts is different from eliminating them.

evidence.title: 2024 Form 10-K, conflicts and business changes
evidence.finding: Goldman discloses continuing actual or potential client conflicts, including its own investments; One Goldman Sachs may increase conflicts. It also reports narrowed consumer activities and remaining principal investments.

claims.next_check: Compare the absolute assertion with risk disclosures and actual transaction structures.

claims.claim: Committing capital for clients deserves a higher earnings multiple than proprietary risk-taking.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Compare business mix, required capital, earnings volatility and valuation on a consistent basis.
claims.reason: This is a relative valuation hypothesis. Fee stability, risk, capital use and price must be specified before a causal premium can be measured.
claims.next_check: Compare business mix, required capital, earnings volatility and valuation on a consistent basis.

claims.claim: One Goldman Sachs substantially improves cross-division collaboration and client service.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Measure cross-selling, retention, client satisfaction and conflicts alongside financial results.
claims.reason: The initiative exists, but Kaplan’s appraisal is an interested management assessment rather than independent evidence of incremental client outcomes.
claims.next_check: Measure cross-selling, retention, client satisfaction and conflicts alongside financial results.

claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
claims.test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.
claims.reason: This is a management judgment and account of Kaplan’s work. It is not a quantified relationship between staffing and returns.
claims.next_check: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.

claims.test: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.
claims.reason: This is a stated aspiration and personal assessment; it does not cancel the firm’s disclosed conflicts or independently verify cultural change.
claims.next_check: Treat as a stated preference or framework; define an observable test before grading an outcome.

claims.claim: Post-crisis capital requirements and stress tests materially changed how large financial firms manage their balance sheets.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

evidence.finding: Aggregate CET1 13.4% at start, hypothetical trough 11.6%; institution-specific outcomes and separate leverage ratios are disclosed. Results reflect scenario, portfolio and model assumptions, not a direct measure of political intent.

claims.claim: Nonbank finance is concerning because it lacks the same bank stress-testing regime.
claims.speaker: Robert Kaplan
